meta.parties: Ruparatne v. Manufacturers Life Insurance Co. of Canada

rules.statement: The action was not time-barred as the refusal to approve payment, which constitutes the breach of contract for prescription purposes, occurred on September 25, 1967, and the plaintiff filed the action on July 3, 1968.
rules.supporting_quote: "Therefore prescription will run from the date of the refusal to pay. When then was the refusal to approve payment? Learned Counsel for the defendant company contends that the letter P6 of 25.4.1958 must be regarded as the refusal to approve cannot be considered, they left the matter open. In P6 itself the defendant company wrote as follows: 'If, however, you can furnish us with proof of death we shall be pleased to look into the matter further.' It will be seen therefore that in P6 there is no unconditional and conclusive refusal. In fact when the plaintiff did submit proof of death in 1965 the defendant Company took more than two years to consider it and eventually on 25.09.1967 wrote P9 to say that their Principals were not satisfied with the claim and denied liability."
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: In terms of Section 6 of our Prescription Ordinance, prescription will begin to run upon breach of the contract.
